How do the risks of injury differ between steady-state cardio and HIIT on a treadmill?

Steady-state cardio, also known as low-intensity cardio, typically involves continuous exercise at a moderate pace that provides a sustained, steady increase in heart rate. This type of exercise is generally considered lower risk for injury because it places less stress on the joints and muscles.

On the other hand, high-intensity interval training (HIIT) involves short bursts of intense exercise followed by slower recovery periods. HIIT may be more challenging due to the high intensity and increased risk of muscular strains, joint stress, and fatigue.
